ideas.behavior_signal: Directed immediate next-item transition distribution P(j|i), with source-specific support count n_i.

ideas.coupling_path: Train transitions create each item's successor target y_i and support weight b_i; the Lorentz distance from y_i to a candidate code's source-role point enters the very energy whose argmin selects that item's RQ code.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Directed successor-flow compatibility will make codes (and therefore SID prefixes) more predictive of next-item continuation than static content-only assignments, improving Stage 3 test Recall@10; retain only if the both-on run beats the matched baseline and the measured train-flow predictability gain is not confined to training metrics.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: Hard RQ code selection during each tokenizer training forward pass, in a behavior-dependent energy that combines content quantization distance and directed-flow compatibility; it therefore changes assignments and assignment gradients.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Lorentz-model geodesic distance d_L on curvature -κ (κ>0), with origin exponential map exp_o for residual/code inputs; learned flow points are projected to the Lorentz hyperboloid.
ideas.key_change: Build a smoothed train-only successor distribution for each item and learn small Lorentzian source/target flow points for items. ideas.leakage_boundary: Freeze transition counts, target-role training data, and b_i using training sequences only; construct validation/test item SIDs by applying the learned tokenizer and frozen train-derived quantities, never by updating graph statistics or assignments from their interactions.
ideas.motivation: Content embeddings can group items by static similarity while ignoring that users move asymmetrically between them; the SID should let the next-item model express directed continuation without making successors indistinguishable from predecessors.
ideas.novelty: Unlike transition-residual quantization, this leaves the residual updates intact and inserts a train-only directed flow potential directly into the discrete code assignment score. Unlike symmetric graph smoothing, incoming and outgoing transition roles remain distinct in a curved Lorentz space.
ideas.observables: Compare per-level code assignments, successor conditional entropy from SID prefixes, train-only held-out-within-train transition NLL diagnostic, and—decisively—Stage 3 test Recall@10 under identical training/evaluation settings; inspect code utilization and assignment churn for instability.
risks: Sparse item transitions make y_i noisy; high-degree successors can dominate; flow and content objectives can conflict, destabilizing assignments; the added code-role points may overfit the training graph or yield no Stage 3 gain. Tune λ on validation only, without using validation interactions to construct SIDs.
ideas.safeguards: Keep κ in a fixed bounded positive range; perform Lorentz calculations in float32 or float64; clamp acosh arguments to at least 1+ε and radicands/denominators; project points back to the future hyperboloid after updates; clip tangent norms before exp maps; use α=1 and a support floor/shrinkage for rare items; normalize weighted target sums with an origin fallback when norm is tiny; cap b_i at 1 and λ modestly; log assignment churn and finite-value checks.
ideas.spec_equations: For train adjacencies, n_ij←count(i→j), n_i=Σ_j n_ij, P_ij=(n_ij+α)/(n_i+αM). Set y_i=normalize_H(Σ_j P_ij v_j), where normalize_H projects the weighted ambient sum onto the future Lorentz sheet. For level residual z_i and candidates c_k, compute x_i=exp_o(z_i), q_k=exp_o(c_k), and E_ik=d_L(x_i,q_k)^2+λb_i d_L(q^src_k,y_i)^2; k*=argmin_k E_ik. Quantize with c_k* and update residual as baseline RQ-VAE. Optimize reconstruction/codebook/commitment objectives as baseline plus selected E behavior term; use straight-through assignment for encoder gradients. Hyperboloid constraint: -X_0²+Σ_{r>0}X_r²=-1/κ and X_0>0. Lorentz distance: d_L(X,Y)=acosh(max(1, -κ⟨X,Y⟩_L))/sqrt(κ).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: frozen training adjacency counts, item residual vectors z_i, RQ code vectors, trainable code source-role and item target-role Lorentz points, λ, κ, and count weights b_i. Output: hard code index k* per item/level and the differentiable selected energy for tokenizer optimization; exported SIDs are the resulting ordinary ordered RQ indices.

specification.text: Let z_i be the current Euclidean residual input at a quantization level and c_k its code vectors. Map normalized z_i and c_k to the Lorentz hyperboloid with curvature -κ using exp_o; denote these points x_i and q_k. From training sequences form P(j|i)=(n_ij+α)/(n_i+α|N|), and a fixed train-only target y_i=normalize(Σ_j P(j|i) v_j), where v_j is a learned target-role Lorentz point. Maintain a learned source-role point u_k per code. For every item/code pair score E(i,k)=d_L(exp_o(z_i),exp_o(c_k))² + λ b_i d_L(exp_{u_k}(0), y_i)², with the second distance evaluated on the hyperboloid after mapping the code source point through exp_o (equivalently use learned hyperboloid code-role points q^src_k); b_i=min(1, log(1+n_i)/log(1+n_95)); assign argmin_k E(i,k), use the ordinary straight-through RQ update/reconstruction loss, and train role points by the same selected-score gradient. More implementably, use learned unit-hyperboloid q^src_k and y_i directly, with second term λ b_i d_L(q^src_k,y_i)^2. Recompute hard assignments each forward pass.

ideas.title: Encode directed next-item flow as Lorentzian code assignment energy

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set η=0 or all u_i=0 while retaining identical Poincare maps, distance, codebooks, schedules, seeds, and parameter count; confirms the branch signal contributes beyond curved quantization.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use train-only successor covariance directions, support weights, Mobius residual transport, and Poincare nearest-code assignment; export resulting SIDs and evaluate Stage3 test Recall@10 once under the locked protocol.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace exp/log, Mobius addition and geodesic distance with Euclidean q_i^ℓ=P r_i^ℓ+ηb_iPu_i and squared Euclidean nearest-code assignment, with matched dimension, η, codebook size, and training schedule.
ideas.behavior_computation: From training-split user sequences only, for every adjacent pair (i,j) collect frozen Stage1 e_j grouped by source item i; compute n_i, mean μ_i and a shrinkage covariance Σ_i=(S_i+λI)/(n_i+λ), where S_i is the centered sum of outer products. Take its leading eigenvector u_i; if n_i<3 or the leading eigengap is below ε, set u_i=0. Keep the training-only arrays fixed for all epochs.
ideas.behavior_signal: User-interest branching: dispersion of the next-item embedding contexts after a given item across distinct training users, rather than raw successor frequency alone.
ideas.cost_estimate: One preprocessing pass over training adjacencies and successor Stage1 vectors: O(E d_e + M d_e²) in a streaming covariance implementation, where E is training adjacency count and M=24,556 items; retain one d_e mean and low-rank branch direction per item. At frozen scale, 24,556 × 24 × 3,000 = 1,768,032,000 item-stage evaluations if every item is visited at each of 24 steps/epoch; practical minibatch work is proportional to actual sampled items. Runtime overhead is one exp/log/Mobius map per sampled item and stage plus the existing O(B K d) distance search, estimated 10–25% tokenizer-step overhead; Stage3 inference overhead is none.
ideas.coupling_equation: q_i^ℓ = exp_0^c(P r_i^ℓ) ⊕_c exp_0^c(η b_i P u_i); k_i^ℓ = argmin_k d_c(q_i^ℓ, exp_0^c(code_k^ℓ))². Here b_i u_i is the named training-behavior branch term and exp_0^c, ⊕_c, d_c are the explicit curved operations.
ideas.coupling_path: Training-user successor dispersion yields u_i and support b_i; the curved map turns ηb_iPu_i into a Poincare point that is Mobius-added to the current mapped residual, changing the very point whose geodesic nearest code defines that SID digit.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: It is worth keeping only if the training users' successor-context dispersion contains repeatable branch directions not already captured by the item text embedding. Observe a changed but stable per-level SID assignment distribution and improved Stage3 test Recall@10, targeting >0.065; check held-out-from-training-user transition predictability only as a diagnostic, not for SID construction or tuning.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In each RQ-VAE residual stage immediately before hard code selection, transport the mapped residual by Mobius-adding a mapped, behavior-derived branch tangent; perform code selection by Poincare geodesic distance and decode the selected point with log_0^c for residual subtraction.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball exponential/logarithmic maps at origin, Mobius addition, and geodesic distance with constant negative curvature -c (c>0).
ideas.key_change: At each residual quantization stage, compute the item-specific branch vector from its train-only successor-context covariance, map the residual and branch vector to the origin tangent space of a negatively curved Poincare ball, and add a bounded branch-directed tangent displacement before the curved nearest-code decision. The displacement modifies the actual point being quantized, so either removing behavior or replacing the curved map changes assignments.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Build the statistics exclusively from the canonical training interaction parquet after applying its train split; never read validation/test rows, targets, or user histories. Stage1 item text embeddings are the frozen pre-existing item features. Generate SIDs for all catalog items by lookup, using zero branch vector for items without a training successor; validation/test are used only in the separately governed Stage3 evaluation.
ideas.motivation: A single item embedding may sit at the junction of distinct user intents (for example, users who consume it as a lead-in to different follow-up categories). An isotropic RQ residual can merge these branches even though their future-use contexts differ.
ideas.novelty: Existing repository mechanisms already use transition-conditioned code scoring, Poincare residual quantization, and successor-branch candidate assignments. This instead derives a per-item branching direction from the dispersion of each training user's next-item contexts and applies it as a tangent-space residual transport before quantization; it is not a code-role transition score or a standalone geometry loss.
ideas.observables: Log per-stage code indices, assignment churn against baseline, distance margins between the best two codes, and downstream Stage3 test Recall@10. With coupling on, branch-heavy items should change assignment more than low-branch items, and their SID prefixes should better predict training-user successor-context branch membership; final success is test Recall@10 >0.065 without test-informed SID changes.
risks: Successor covariance can be noisy for low-support items, top eigenvectors can be unstable or nearly isotropic, and branch displacement may damage semantic reconstruction or overfit frequent users. Capping b_i, shrinkage, a small η, and reporting support-stratified assignment churn mitigate these risks.
ideas.safeguards: Compute statistics in float64 or streaming covariance; eigengap/support gate and zero-vector fallback for unsupported items; normalize eigenvectors with deterministic sign; clamp norms to (1−ε)/√c before ball operations, clamp atanh inputs to 1−ε, use stable small-norm series for exp/log, constrain η and P spectral norm, use float32 minimum for distance accumulation, and assert all outputs finite. Tune η and shrinkage on training-only diagnostics or validation under the project's prescribed model-selection protocol, never on test Recall.
ideas.spec_equations: For each training adjacency i→j, accumulate μ_i=Σe_j/n_i and S_i=Σ(e_j−μ_i)(e_j−μ_i)^T; Σ_i=(S_i+λI)/(n_i+λ). Let u_i be the principal unit eigenvector when support/eigengap passes thresholds, otherwise 0; b_i=min(1,log(1+n_i)/log(1+n_95)). For each level: x=exp_0^c(P r); a=exp_0^c(η b_i P u_i); q=x⊕_c a; k*=argmin_k d_c(q,exp_0^c(c_k))²; v=log_0^c(exp_0^c(c_k*)); r←r−v. Use baseline straight-through quantized forward path and losses. Poincare formulas: exp_0^c(v)=tanh(√c||v||)v/(√c||v||); x⊕_c y=((1+2c<x,y>+c||y||²)x+(1−c||x||²)y)/(1+2c<x,y>+c²||x||²||y||²); d_c(x,y)=2/√c atanh(√c||−x⊕_c y||); log_0^c(x)=atanh(√c||x||)x/(√c||x||).
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: canonical training user sequences, frozen item embeddings e_i, stage residual r_i^ℓ, learned projection P, codebooks, c, η, and shrinkage/support thresholds. Outputs: fixed per-item (u_i,b_i) training-only branch statistics and per-level hard code index k_i^ℓ; exported ordered code indices form each item's SID.

specification.text: Let sequences be the ordered user interactions in the training split only. For item i, collect successor items j from adjacent training events, embed each j using frozen Stage1 vector e_j, and compute μ_i and covariance Σ_i over those vectors; define b_i=min(1, log(1+n_i)/log(1+n_95)) and let u_i be the unit top eigenvector of Σ_i, with sign fixed by positive dot product with the mean successor vector. For level ℓ with Euclidean residual r_i^ℓ, map x_i^ℓ=exp_0^c(P r_i^ℓ) and a_i=exp_0^c(η b_i P u_i), where P is a learned low-rank projection into dimension d and c>0 is fixed. Form the target q_i^ℓ=x_i^ℓ ⊕_c a_i (Mobius addition), select k*=argmin_k d_c(q_i^ℓ, exp_0^c(code^ℓ_k))², and map selected code back with log_0^c before baseline Euclidean residual subtraction. Train with baseline reconstruction/codebook/commitment losses through the straight-through assignment. Freeze branch statistics before RQ-VAE training.

ideas.title: Route user-interest branches into hyperbolic residual updates

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set lambda=0 (same curved RQ-VAE, same schedule and seeds); branch statistics are not used.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use the complete branch-conditioned Poincare assignment; compare all arms with matched Stage3 training and validation selection.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace Poincare maps/geodesic with Euclidean vectors and squared Euclidean distance while retaining the exact branch penalty direction/projection; retune only a predeclared lambda grid.
ideas.behavior_computation: Training split only: collect (user, preceding up-to-5 distinct item IDs, next target item) transitions; map history items to frozen Stage1 embeddings, mean-pool and project; cluster contexts per target into at most 8 branches, with minimum support 3, then compute count-weighted covariance. No held-out sequence is included.
ideas.behavior_signal: User-interest branching among contexts that precede the same target item.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute sparse context summaries in O(number of training transitions); first-level assignment adds one scalar projection and cost term per item-codeword pair. At frozen scale 24,556 items and 24 steps/epoch, a full-item pass per step means about 24,556* K0 projections (K0=64: 1.57M scalar projections/step) and 72,000 steps over 3,000 epochs; cache item branch vectors/eigenvectors so only the inexpensive pairwise projection is added. Expected wall-clock overhead 5–15% versus the same curved baseline, excluding one-time sparse aggregation.
ideas.coupling_path: Training-only branch covariance supplies h_j and direction u_j inside the same per-codeword curved assignment score; removing behaviour eliminates g, while replacing d_c/log/exp by Euclidean geometry changes the score and assignments.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Items with genuine multi-intent use have behaviour branches that are not aligned with text-only nearest-code boundaries; branch-conditioned geodesic assignment should alter their first-token assignments and make next-token prefixes more predictive. Keep only if both-on improves validation-selected Stage3 test Recall@10 and exceeds 0.065, with reproducible seeds.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: First residual-quantization level's hard codeword assignment during Stage2 fitting; the codeword vectors and encoded items are mapped to the ball before computing the behaviour-conditioned cost.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare-ball exp_0^c/log_0^c and geodesic distance d_c for fixed negative curvature -c, c=1 initially.
ideas.key_change: Build training-only user-context branches and estimate a compact tangent-space branch prototype and dispersion for each item. During first-level quantization, use dispersion to modulate a Poincare geodesic cost between the encoded item and each codeword, so branch-rich items are assigned by a behaviour-conditioned curved metric; later residual levels stay baseline.
ideas.leakage_boundary: Generate statistics solely from the Stage2 training interaction split and the fixed Stage1 item embeddings; persist item-indexed statistics before SID fitting. Validation/test events are not read by preprocessing, assignment, checkpoint selection for SID, or cached statistics.
ideas.motivation: A single semantic prefix can merge items that are substitutes for one audience but lead into distinct next-step intents for different users; preserve branching recommendation roles while retaining text-semantic reconstruction.
ideas.novelty: Rather than append a behavioural token or regularize an independent graph loss, user-specific branching changes the curved distance that determines each item's first RQ assignment. It uses per-item dispersion over user-context branch directions, not global popularity balancing or a generic hyperbolic RQ-VAE.
ideas.observables: First-level SID changes concentrated on high-branch items; increased training-prefix predictability measured on held-out training contexts; Stage3 validation/test Recall@10 should rise, with target test Recall@10 >0.065.
risks: Sparse per-item sequences make branch covariance noisy; the leading direction can capture popularity or sequence-position artifacts; lambda can overwhelm semantic reconstruction; freezing the branch statistics may miss evolving assignments.
ideas.safeguards: Clamp sqrt(c)||x|| <= 1-epsilon before exp/log; clamp atanh input to 1-epsilon; normalize u_j and set it to zero for fewer than 3 contexts or near-zero covariance; cap alpha and lambda; accumulate statistics in float64, costs in float32; use deterministic clustering seed and stable tie-breaking.
ideas.spec_equations: Given tangent vectors a_j,v_k with norm bounded below 1/sqrt(c), exp_0^c(x)=tanh(sqrt(c)||x||)x/(sqrt(c)||x||), log_0^c(y)=atanh(sqrt(c)||y||)y/(sqrt(c)||y||), d_c(x,y)=2/sqrt(c)*atanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)oplus_c y||). Use branch covariance C_j=sum_b p_jb(m_jb-m_j)(m_jb-m_j)^T, h_j=clip(tr(C_j)/(tr(C_j)+tau),0,1), u_j=top_eigenvector(C_j). Assignment uses S above, with deterministic tie-break by code index; backprop through selected code via standard straight-through estimator.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: training-only transition records, frozen item embeddings, Stage2 encoder output a_j, first-level tangent codewords v_k, c, lambda, alpha. Outputs: per-item branch statistics (h_j,u_j) and first-level code index k*(j), then ordinary residual codes.

specification.text: For each training user sequence, form contexts from the preceding up-to-5 distinct items and target next item j. Encode context by the mean of frozen item embeddings, project to tangent space at origin, and cluster contexts into B=8 fixed k-means branch prototypes per target item (retain counts n_jb). Let h_j be the normalized weighted covariance trace of these branch vectors, clipped to [0,1]. With z_j=exp_0^c(a_j), codewords q_k=exp_0^c(v_k), define d_k=d_c(z_j,q_k), and g_jk=log(1+alpha*h_j*|<log_0(z_j)-log_0(q_k), u_j>|), where u_j is the leading eigenvector of the branch covariance (zero if undefined). Assign k*=argmin_k [d_k^2 + lambda*g_jk]; train reconstruction/codebook losses using that hard assignment and straight-through gradient. This is a curved, behaviour-conditioned assignment cost, not a post-hoc loss.

ideas.title: User-branch-conditioned hyperbolic first-code assignment

ideas.ablation_behavior_off: Set eta_l=0 at every level, leaving the same Poincare RQ-VAE and all other losses unchanged.
ideas.ablation_both_on: Use transition-derived b_i and Poincare residual displacement/assignment/subtraction throughout; train and evaluate the same Stage3 pipeline.
ideas.ablation_geometry_off: Replace exp/log/Mobius operations and d_c with Euclidean vector addition/subtraction and squared Euclidean distance, retaining identical transition distributions, gates, eta schedule, and codebook sizes.
ideas.behavior_computation: On Stage2 training interactions only, count adjacent distinct items within each user's ordered sequence; divide transition counts by source row sum after multiplying each edge count by (1+target training frequency)^-0.5; retain top 32 outgoing targets and normalize. Create barycenters from frozen Stage1 embeddings mapped into the fixed-curvature ball.
ideas.behavior_signal: Popularity-adjusted directed next-item transition distribution for each item.
ideas.cost_estimate: Precompute truncated outgoing distributions/barycenters in O(E_train log 32) and store one tangent vector per item. Each RQ level adds one log-map/geodesic step per item and a scalar gate; pairwise codeword distance remains baseline complexity. At 24,556 items, 24 steps/epoch, 3,000 epochs (72,000 steps), cache b_i and compute the per-item flow once per quantizer forward; expected 10–25% overhead depending on latent dimension and number of residual levels.
ideas.coupling_path: The row-normalized training transition distribution determines b_i; b_i enters the Poincare log/exp residual displacement; the displaced curved point is the actual input to the codeword argmin. Removing either makes a different residual and SID.
ideas.falsifiable_hypothesis: Directed consumption flow has a useful local tangent direction not recoverable from static item text; steering residual quantization toward that direction should shift residual SIDs to encode successor-relevant distinctions and raise Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
ideas.hyperbolic_location: In every residual quantization level of Stage2: the current residual is geometrically displaced toward its training-only outgoing barycenter before code assignment, and residual subtraction returns through the curved log map.
ideas.hyperbolic_operator: Poincare exp/log maps, parallel point displacement via exp_R, Mobius subtraction, and geodesic distance with fixed curvature -c (c=1).
ideas.key_change: Estimate each item's popularity-adjusted outgoing transition barycenter from training sequences, then at each RQ level move the current residual a small fraction along the Poincare log-map direction toward that barycenter. Quantize the moved residual by Poincare distance and subtract the chosen codeword using the same curved residual operation.
ideas.leakage_boundary: The transition matrix is built only from training users' training-period adjacent pairs. Item frequencies, neighbour lists, and barycenters are frozen before tokenizer fitting; no validation/test sequence, target, frequency, or model output participates.
ideas.motivation: Text reconstruction alone can spend residual capacity on distinctions that do not help predict what users consume next; directed training transitions provide an explicit recommendation-oriented direction for residual code selection.
ideas.novelty: Unlike graph-neighbour reweighting of ordinary nearest-neighbour VQ, transition flow is transported into the Poincare tangent space and steers the residual along a curved geodesic before each residual quantization decision. It modifies the residual state itself, so behaviour and geometry cannot be separated into unrelated losses.
ideas.observables: Residual digits should change more for items with confident outgoing distributions; held-out prefix-to-next-item accuracy and Stage3 Recall@10 should improve. Main target is Stage3 test Recall@10 >0.065, compared at matched validation selection.
risks: Flow may encode popularity rather than conditional preference; outgoing neighbours can be noisy for low-degree items; repeated steering can distort reconstruction or erase useful semantics; Frechet-mean approximation in a tangent chart may be biased for broad neighbourhoods.
ideas.safeguards: Project ball points to norm <=(1-epsilon)/sqrt(c); clamp atanh arguments; clip tangent norms before exp; if no outgoing transition set eta=0; smooth popularity with +1; cap neighbour probabilities and eta (initial eta <=0.1); detach cached barycenters; monitor reconstruction and flow displacement norms for divergence; use fixed seed and identical preprocessing in geometry-off arm.
ideas.spec_equations: For curvature -c, Mobius addition x opplus_c y=((1+2c<x,y>+c||y||^2)x+(1-c||x||^2)y)/(1+2c<x,y>+c^2||x||^2||y||^2); d_c(x,y)=2/sqrt(c)*atanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)oplus_c y||); log_x(y)=2/(sqrt(c)*lambda_x)*atanh(sqrt(c)||(-x)oplus_c y||)*((-x)oplus_c y), lambda_x=2/(1-c||x||^2); exp_x(v)=x opplus_c [tanh(sqrt(c)*lambda_x||v||/2)*v/(sqrt(c)||v||)]. Use these formulae for displacement and assignment; use tangent residual norm clipping.
ideas.spec_inputs_outputs: Inputs: train-only ordered user sequences, frozen item embeddings, encoder outputs, per-item outgoing distribution P_i, tangent codebooks at each level, curvature c and eta_l. Outputs: first-level and residual SID indices, plus reconstructed embedding for the standard RQ-VAE losses.

specification.text: From training directed counts A_ij, set P_ij=(A_ij+eps)/(sum_l A_il+eps*|N(i)|), retaining at most 32 outgoing neighbours by P_ij; downweight each count by target popularity^-0.5 before row normalization. Let b_i be the Poincare weighted Frechet-mean approximation exp_0^c(sum_j P_ij log_0^c(z_j)), z_j=exp_0^c(enc(x_j)). For item i at level l, residual r_l in tangent coordinates maps to R_l=exp_0^c(r_l); compute flow f_i=log_{R_l}(b_i), clip norm, and set R'_l=exp_{R_l}^c(eta_l * sigmoid(s_i) * f_i), where s_i=log(1+outdegree_i). Choose k_l=argmin_k d_c(R'_l, exp_0^c(v_lk))^2; update R_{l+1}=log_0^c((-q_lk)oplus_c R'_l), where q_lk=exp_0^c(v_lk). Use straight-through assignment and baseline reconstruction plus commitment losses.

ideas.title: Transition-flow geodesic residual quantization

assumptions: Each train.parquet history is chronological and contains only preceding training interactions for its row's target; directed transitions are formed from adjacent history entries followed by that target, without validation/test data.
